newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Deal removes threat to NZ Bluff oyster season.
newsitem.headline: Deal removes threat to NZ Bluff oyster season.

text.p: A last minute out of court settlement between the government and the Treaty of Waitangi Fisheries Commission has cleared the way for the start of this winter's Bluff oyster season, Fisheries Minister John Luxton said on Monday.
"With this settlement the oyster season can now get underway with certainty. We can now get on with the important job of continuing to sustainably manage this fishery," Luxton said in a statement.
The government has agreed to acquire quota to 20 percent of New Zealand's best-known seafood delicacy, which it will transfer to Maori.
A court hearing to resolve a dispute between the government and the commission, which holds fishing assets granted to Maori prior to distribution, had been set down for later on Monday.
The purchase is likely to cost the government around $6 million.
A spokesman for Luxton said the tender process was being completed now.
The settlement is part of a 1992 agreement to transfer to Maori 20 percent of all new species brought under the quota management system (QMS).
The commission initiated court action because of delays in transferring the Bluff oysters to the QMS.
As part of the settlement, the government has agreed to transfer other new species into the management system "as soon as practicable".
Luxton said the settlement meant Maori will have access to the Foveaux Strait oyster fishery from June 1, 1997 -- before the fishery is introduced to the QMS system.
